# Central Shenandoah Planning District Commission
## About us
The Central Shenandoah Planning District Commission (CSPDC) provides planning services and technical assistance to its member jurisdictions including; comprehensive and land use planning, transportation, water and waste water utilities, natural resource management, solid waste management, affordable housing, economic and community development, disaster mitigation and preparedness education, and human services. Member jurisdictions include the Counties of Augusta, Bath, Highland, Rockbridge, and Rockingham, and the Cities of Buena Vista, Harrisonburg, Lexington, Staunton, and Waynesboro and eleven towns. Cooperative solutions to problems are addressed at the Central Shenandoah Planning District Commission through regional efforts and partnerships with our local jurisdictions and other stakeholders.

# Contact:
Chase Sawyer
[chase.sawyer@dhcd.virginia.gov](mailto:chase.sawyer@dhcd.virginia.gov)
Pursuant to the Regional Cooperation Act, Virginia has 21 planning district commissions (PDCs), voluntary associations of local governments intended to foster intergovernmental cooperation by bringing together local elected and appointed officials and involved citizens to discuss common needs and determine solutions to regional issues. Another purpose of PDCs is to encourage and facilitate local government cooperation in addressing, on a regional basis, problems of greater than local significance. This is accomplished through the development of a regional strategic plan and through the various other duties assigned to PDCs in the Regional Cooperation Act.
VIRGINIA PDCS
Virginia Association of Planning District Commissions
Region 1 – LENOWISCO Planning District Commission
Region 2 – Cumberland Plateau Planning District Commission
Region 3 – Mount Rogers Planning District Commission
Region 4 – New River Valley Regional Commission
Region 5 – Roanoke Valley-Alleghany Regional Commission
Region 6 – Central Shenandoah Planning District Commission
Region 7 – Northern Shenandoah Valley Regional Commission
Region 8 – Northern Virginia Regional Commission

Region 22 – Accomack-Northampton Planning District Commission

CODE OF VIRGINIA

# Contact:
Section 15.2-4215 requires each PDC to submit an annual report to its member local governments and the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) on how the PDC has met the provisions of the Regional Cooperation Act. Further, §36-139.6 provides that DHCD is to submit a biennial report to the governor and General Assembly, as well as certain other state agencies, which includes findings as to compliance by PDCs with the Regional Cooperation Act. In support of their required duties and pursuant to §36-139.6, the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) distributes state general appropriation funding for each PDC.

## How a Christmas tree permit works
Most national forests sell their Christmas tree permits online through Recreation.gov, and some ranger district offices sell them over the counter. One permit covers one tree, cut in the areas and on the dates the forest names, and across the forests below the price runs $5 to $20 a tree. Each forest sets its own tree size, species and household limits, printed with the permit.
> Purchase your Christmas tree permit in advance of your visit to the forest in your area.
Recreation.gov, read September 22, 2026. Read it at the source
> Each forest will have specific guidelines and season dates for cutting a holiday tree.
Recreation.gov. Read it at the source

## How a Christmas tree permit works
### The online fee
Recreation.gov adds a reservation fee to each online permit. Green Mountain National Forest prints both numbers together:
> Permits cost $5.00 per tree (a $2.50 Recreation.gov reservation fee will be applied).
Green Mountain National Forest, on Recreation.gov. Read it at the source

## How a Christmas tree permit works
### The free permit for fourth graders
A fourth grader with an Every Kid Outdoors pass can get a free Christmas tree permit from a national forest. The pass is free too, from the Every Kid Outdoors program, and the permit is redeemed on Recreation.gov with the pass number.
> Every Kid Outdoors pass holders are also eligible for a free holiday tree permit through their local National Forest. To obtain a free holiday tree permit, visit Recreation.gov to apply using the Every Kid Outdoors pass by checking the box indicating you have a pass and entering the pass or voucher number (a $2.50 reservation fee will be applied).
Green Mountain National Forest, on Recreation.gov. Read it at the source

## How a Christmas tree permit works
Most national forests sell their Christmas tree permits online through Recreation.gov, and some ranger district offices sell them over the counter. One permit covers one tree, cut in the areas and on the dates the forest names, and across the forests below the price runs $5 to $20 a tree. Each forest sets its own tree size, species and household limits, printed with the permit.
> Purchase your Christmas tree permit in advance of your visit to the forest in your area.

> Each forest will have specific guidelines and season dates for cutting a holiday tree.
Recreation.gov. Read it at the source

## How a Christmas tree permit works
### The online fee
Recreation.gov adds a reservation fee to each online permit. Green Mountain National Forest prints both numbers together:
> Permits cost $5.00 per tree (a $2.50 Recreation.gov reservation fee will be applied).
Green Mountain National Forest, on Recreation.gov. Read it at the source

## How a Christmas tree permit works
### The free permit for fourth graders
A fourth grader with an Every Kid Outdoors pass can get a free Christmas tree permit from a national forest. The pass is free too, from the Every Kid Outdoors program, and the permit is redeemed on Recreation.gov with the pass number.
> Every Kid Outdoors pass holders are also eligible for a free holiday tree permit through their local National Forest. To obtain a free holiday tree permit, visit Recreation.gov to apply using the Every Kid Outdoors pass by checking the box indicating you have a pass and entering the pass or voucher number (a $2.50 reservation fee will be applied).
